project.name: Authority Checkout
project.tagline: One execution-scoped authority artifact for runtime assembly and human inspection — with explicit freshness, trust provenance and effect-gate limits.

research_question: Can one task-scoped derived authority artifact serve both runtime assembly and human reasoning, remain honest when upstream state changes, preserve which inputs may define authority, and avoid treating human approval as deterministic enforcement?
core_principles: runtime and human inspection consume the same artifact
live or invalidating upstream state must not be silently frozen
mixed-trust context may influence reasoning but may not expand authority
human approval is not equivalent to deterministic policy
policy-resolvable effects should be determinized before escalation

effect_gate_model.invariant: EG-01: human approval is not a deterministic security control unless decision quality remains acceptable under realistic approval load.
effect_gate_model.design_hypothesis: Deterministically decidable policy should produce machine allow/deny; human review should be reserved for genuine ambiguity.

prototypes.03: Break the Checkout adversarial proof room

adversarial_invariants.AC-04: prove human view and runtime do not consume the same artifact
adversarial_invariants.AC-07: exhaust the reviewer until a prohibited effect is approved

known_challenges: hostile-influenced context crossing into authority derivation
approval fatigue turning human effect gates into rubber stamps
claims_not_to_make: Authority Checkout replaces IAM, APS, OAuth, Purview, policy engines, sandboxes or capability systems

next_phase.name: evidence runs before more architecture
next_phase.goal: Run people and external LLMs against Prototypes 01.1, 04, 05 and 06 through Break the Checkout before adding another conceptual layer.
next_phase.parallel_blocker: Resolve APS positioning as upstream delegation semantics versus rival before building delegation trace.
